newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ PM says parties want tight spending controls.
newsitem.headline: NZ PM says parties want tight spending controls.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Monday said nobody was arguing against tight fiscal controls in the current coalition negotiations.

At an earlier press conference New Zealand First leader Wisnton Peters, whose party holds the balance of power, said it was inevitable there would be more spending and a wider inflation target band than the current 0-2 percent, whichever parties formed a government.
"Most parties campaigned on additional spending. I guess he is making his comments on that basis," Bolger said of Peters' comments as he headed into the eighth round of talks.
"I'm sure nobody is arguing there shouldn't be tight controls. It is a question of what comes out of the discussions in the formation of a coalition government."
Bolger would not comment on Reserve Bank governor Don Brash's comments on Monday that the July 1997 tax cut package may have to be deferred if a new government opts for more spending.
"That is Dr Brash's view I am not discussing that. I am going into coalition talks." Bolger said.

Asked about NZ First's policy of using the planned $1.1 billion second round of tax cuts, planned for next July, as the basis for a new compulsory superannuation fund, Bolger said: "All these are at the heart of the discussions that have been ongoing at the moment."
Bolger also declined to comment on Peters' statement that it was inevitable the inflation target would be widened.
NZ First is running parallel talks with National and Labour over the shape of the next government.
Parliament must meet no later than December 13, but the leaders of the three parties to the talks have said a decision on the new government may not be reached by then.
